object: TO STUDY THE HYDROLYSIS OF SOME NORMAL SALTS
Hydrolysis of a salt is defined as the combination of ions of the salt with hydrogen and hydroxyl ions of water to give acidic or basic solution.
Salts of strong acid and weak base (e.g. NH4Cl) are hydrolysed to give weakly acidic solution whereas salts of weak acid and strong base (e.g.

Na2C03) are hydrolysed to give weakly alkaline solution. Salts of weak acid and weak base (e.g. CH3COONH4) are hydrolysed to give almost neutral solutions. Salts of strong acid and strong base (e.g. NaCl) are not hydrolysed and therefore, their solutions are neutral. The acidic, alkaline or neutral nature can be identified with the help of the indicators like litmus papers, phenolphthalein solution, methyl orange solution etc.

Methyl orange solution produces pink colour with an acid whereas it produces light yellow colour with a base. (Phenolphthalein gives a pink colour with alkali and it has no colour with acid. Acid turns blue litmus to red and base turns red litmus to blue).
